report:
## Conclusion: The claim is well-supported by high-quality evidence

Add-on cannabidiol (CBD) reduces convulsive seizure frequency in children with Dravet syndrome, and this is now established through multiple randomized controlled trials, not just anecdote.

**Key evidence:**

1. **Pivotal RCT (Devinsky et al., NEJM 2017):** In a double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of 120 children/young adults with Dravet syndrome and drug-resistant seizures, add-on CBD (20 mg/kg/day) reduced median convulsive-seizure frequency by 38.9% vs. 13.3% with placebo (p=0.01). CBD also increased the proportion of patients with ≥50% seizure reduction. Adverse events (somnolence, diarrhea, vomiting, fatigue, elevated liver enzymes) were more common with CBD (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1611618).

2. **Dose-ranging trial (JAMA Neurology, 2020):** A second randomized trial (n=199) compared CBD 10 mg/kg/day, 20 mg/kg/day, and placebo, confirming efficacy at both doses with a better tolerability profile at the lower dose, reinforcing the dose-response relationship (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/379048758_The_efficacy_and_safety_of_cannabidiol_CBD_in_pediatric_patients_with_Dravet_Syndrome_a_narrative_review_of_clinical_trials).

3. **Regulatory confirmation:** Based on this trial evidence, the FDA approved Epidiolex (pharmaceutical-grade CBD) specifically as add-on therapy for seizures in Dravet syndrome (and Lennox-Gastaut syndrome) in patients ≥2 years old, requiring rigorous efficacy and safety review (https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-approvals-and-databases/drug-trials-snapshots-epidiolex).

4. **Real-world safety data:** Post-marketing FAERS analysis confirms the drug's adverse event profile seen in trials, with hepatic enzyme elevation and GI/sedative effects being the most notable concerns (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S1876201823003854).

**Bottom line:** This is a well-replicated, FDA-validated finding — one of the strongest evidence bases for a cannabis-derived therapy in medicine.
